The board lives in an admin app; you are doing a quality/completeness audit.

Read the full board dump at: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/board-dump.txt

Focus ONLY on these columns: "Competitor Teardowns", "Market & Users", "Differentiation & Moat", "Risks & Pitfalls", "MVP & Roadmap". (You may skim other columns for context/overlap, but only audit these.)

Key context you should hold: unit economics is the existential risk (LLM token tax caps margins; "never sell flat/unlimited AI compute"); #1 category weakness is credit/bill-shock; Hostinger Horizons is the closest analog; security-by-default is a differentiator; Kodely depends on a funded Anthropic API key.

Produce a CONCISE, structured report:
1. IMPROVE — specific existing cards that are weak, outdated, vague, or wrong, and exactly how to sharpen them (reference card titles).
2. ADD — genuinely missing cards this area should have (title + one-line rationale each). Only real gaps, not padding.
3. ISSUES — redundant/duplicate cards, miscategorized cards, or stale assumptions.
4. TOP 5 — the 5 highest-leverage items (improve or add) in your area, ranked.

Be specific and terse. Return only the report as text (it becomes my data, not a user message). No preamble.

1	KODELY BOARD DUMP — 653 cards, 23 columns
2	
3	
4	============================================================
5	COLUMN: Competitor Teardowns  (95 cards)
6	============================================================
7	
8	[HIGH/IDEA] What rocket.new is: "Vibe Solutioning" platform
9	Rocket.new positions itself as the "world's first Vibe Solutioning platform" — not just an AI app builder. It bundles three pillars into one shared-context workspace: **Solve** (market research, idea validation, PRDs, competitor mapping), **Build** (generate production-ready web + mobile apps), and **Intelligence** (continuous 24/7 competitor monitoring, daily briefings). This 'strategy-before-code' framing is its core differentiator vs. Lovable/Bolt, which jump straight to generation. Source: https://www.rocket.new/ and https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction
10	
11	[NORMAL/IDEA] Company: DhiWise → Rocket pivot, $15M seed
12	Rocket.new is the rebrand of **DhiWise**, founded April 2021 in Surat, India by Vishal Virani, Rahul Shingala, and Deepak Dhanak. DhiWise raised ~$9.5M (Series A led by Accel). It rebranded to Rocket in **September 2025**, went AI-first, relocated HQ to Palo Alto, and raised a **$15M seed** led by Salesforce Ventures with Accel, India Quotient, and Together Fund. Sources: https://techcrunch.com/2022/08/22/dhiwise-takes-the-tedium-out-of-programming/ , https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/dhiwise
13	
14	[HIGH/IDEA] Traction signals: 400K users, 500K apps, $4.5M ARR
15	Within ~3 months of the June 2025 beta launch Rocket reportedly crossed **400,000+ users** across **180 countries**, generated **500,000+ applications**, hit **$4.5M ARR** with **10,000+ paid subscribers**. Enterprise logos claimed include Meta, PayPal, KPMG, and PwC. These are self-reported PR numbers — treat with caution, but they indicate fast growth Kodely is competing against. Source: https://www.producthunt.com/stories/from-golden-kitty-to-10m-raised and productgrowth.in review
16	
17	[HIGH/IDEA] Workflow: prompt → full-stack app in one shot
18	Rocket treats every prompt as a **full-stack build instruction** — a single natural-language prompt (or Figma frame / screenshot / Notion doc) generates screens, navigation, data model, and design together, aiming to avoid iterative rounds ('one-shot' mode). It then generates frontend + backend + DB schema + auth + API endpoints + file storage simultaneously. Users iterate afterward via chat or the visual editor. Source: https://www.rocket.new/ai-app-builder and https://www.rocket.new/blog/best-ai-prompts-for-one-shot-app-generation-guide-this-year
19	
20	[HIGH/IDEA] Generated tech stack: Next.js web, Flutter mobile, Supabase
21	Web apps are generated as **Next.js (React/TypeScript)**; mobile apps as **Flutter** (iOS + Android). The default backend is **Supabase** — bundling PostgreSQL, auth (email/password + Google/GitHub social), row-level security, file storage, and edge functions. Auth, DB schemas, and REST endpoints are auto-generated. This opinionated stack is a key contrast point for Kodely's own stack choice. Sources: https://docs.rocket.new/integrations/supabase , https://www.rocket.new/build
22	
23	[HIGH/IDEA] Deploys to Netlify (third-party hosting dependency)
24	Despite marketing 'Rocket-hosted infrastructure', the docs reveal web apps actually deploy to **Netlify** with a public URL via the 'Launch' button, and **custom domains require connecting your own Netlify account**. Mobile builds get a mobile-optimized web preview link. This reliance on external hosting is a strategic opening for Kodely, which owns its VPS/hosting stack and can offer first-party hosting. Source: https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq
25	
26	[HIGH/IDEA] Trustpilot: 3.3/5 across ~60 reviews (polarized)
27	Rocket.new holds a **TrustScore of 3.3/5 from ~60 reviews** on Trustpilot — 'Average', notably lower than typical SaaS. Experiences are highly polarized: praise for bringing ideas to life fast and helpful support, versus complaints about cost and bugs. The mediocre score despite huge user numbers signals real retention/satisfaction risk. Source: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/rocket.new
28	
29	[URGENT/IDEA] #1 Complaint: credits burn fast, builds get expensive
30	The dominant complaint across Trustpilot/reviews: **credits are consumed very quickly** and building a fully functional app routinely requires buying extra credits. One user reported spending **$250 on credits**; testimonials cite ~**200k 'credits' for a mobile app build**. Non-technical users report 'credits running out before meaningful features ship', making cost unpredictable. This is the single biggest wedge for Kodely to undercut. Source: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/rocket.new
31	
32	[URGENT/IDEA] #2 Complaint: fixing Rocket's own bugs costs more credits
33	Reviewers describe the platform as 'half-baked' with unstable workflows: prompting it to fix an issue often introduces new problems, and **fixing bugs the platform itself created consumes additional credits**. This 'pay-to-fix-its-own-mistakes' loop is the most damaging recurring criticism. Kodely should design so error correction / self-heal iterations are cheap or free. Source: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/rocket.new
34	
35	[NORMAL/IDEA] Strength: pre-build 'Solve' intelligence layer
36	Rocket's genuine differentiator is the **Solve phase** that runs before code: market research, competitive landscape mapping, problem validation, and a structured strategic brief (exportable as PDF/PPTX). Competitors (Lovable, Bolt, Replit) have no equivalent strategy/research layer. If Kodely competes purely on build, this is where Rocket claims an edge worth neutralizing or matching. Source: https://www.rocket.new/blog/rocket-new-vs-bolt-vs-replit-the-difference-that-precedes-build-over-code-quality
37	
38	[NORMAL/IDEA] Strength: 'production-grade' code you own + Intelligence
39	Rocket markets clean, production-grade code that 'belongs entirely to you', with SEO optimization, accessibility, responsive layouts, and modular architecture built into the first generation — positioning against Lovable/Bolt as 'apps not prototypes'. The **Intelligence** pillar (ongoing competitor monitoring + daily briefings) is a retention/recurring-value hook competitors lack. Source: https://www.rocket.new/blog/rocket-new-vs-lovable-which-builds-production-ready-apps-not-prototypes
40	
41	[NORMAL/IDEA] Positioning vs Lovable / Bolt / Replit
42	In head-to-heads Rocket frames rivals as fast but shallow: Lovable = fast build, no pre-build intelligence/memory; Bolt = fast, clean frontend scaffolding for devs but no strategy layer or precision editing; Replit = coding control focus. Rocket's pitch is 'strategy + full-stack + continuous intelligence in one'. Independent comparisons (SourceForge/Slashdot) note Bolt is faster/simpler while Rocket claims cleaner architecture and scaling control. Sources: https://sourceforge.net/software/compare/Bolt.new-vs-Lovable-vs-Rocket.new/ , rocket.new blog
43	
44	[NORMAL/IDEA] Weakness: mobile publishing is high-friction
45	Flutter mobile apps can be downloaded as **APK for Android testing**, but **iOS requires downloading source code and building locally in Xcode** with an Apple Developer account ($99/yr); Google Play submission needs the one-time $25 fee. So 'build a mobile app from a prompt' still dumps non-technical users into native toolchains to actually ship. A real gap Kodely can either match honestly or improve. Source: https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq
46	
47	[NORMAL/IDEA] Weakness: GitHub two-way sync limited to Next.js TS
48	GitHub **two-way sync** (push to repo + pull external changes back in) is only supported for **Next.js TypeScript** projects, and **source-code download requires a paid plan (Pro+)**. Flutter/mobile and free-tier users are more locked in. Export limitations are a common lock-in grievance Kodely can differentiate on by offering full export earlier. Source: https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq
49	
50	[HIGH/IDEA] Credit/token economics are opaque
51	Neither the pricing page nor docs publish a **credit-to-action conversion** (how many messages/edits = 1 credit). Guidance is only qualitative ('clear prompts use fewer credits, vague ones use more'). Combined with the 'buy more credits' pressure, this opacity is a recurring trust complaint. Kodely can win goodwill with transparent, predictable usage metering. Source: https://docs.rocket.new/get-started/pricing-plans , https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq
52	
53	[LOW/IDEA] Enterprise/compliance posture
54	Rocket advertises SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, and CCPA compliance, plus SAML/SSO, audit logs, data localization, and premium support via a 'contact sales' enterprise track. This signals they're chasing upmarket/enterprise buyers alongside indie builders. Kodely should know the compliance bar for any enterprise-facing positioning. Source: https://www.rocket.new/build
55

Built by Maor Shlomo as a solo side project — only 6 employees and zero external funding when **Wix acquired it for $80M in June 2025** (earn-outs to 2029). Now the engine behind Wix's app-building push. Strength: astonishing capital efficiency and product-market fit; Weakness: post-acquisition it is being folded into Wix's ecosystem, reducing independence. Source: https://www.wix.com/press-room/home/post/wix-further-expands-into-vibe-coding-with-acquisition-of-base44-a-hyper-growth-startup-that-simplif
196	
197	[URGENT/IDEA] Hostinger Horizons (closest analog to Kodely)
198	No-code AI web-app builder from a hosting company — the single closest strategic analog to Kodely. Describe an app in plain language; it generates code, auto-fixes errors, and includes **free hosting + free email** baked in. Tiered by AI messages: Explorer $9.99 (30 msgs), Starter $19.99 (70), Hobbyist $55.99 (200), plus a Hustler tier; 7-day free trial, buy extra credits. Strength: hosting+email bundling makes it a true all-in-one for its price; Weakness: message-metered plans feel stingy and complex apps outgrow it fast. **Study this pricing/bundle model directly.** Source: https://www.hostinger.com/horizons/features
199	
200	[HIGH/IDEA] GoDaddy Airo (agentic, incumbent)
201	GoDaddy launched **Airo.ai in Nov 2025** as an agentic AI that turns a conversation into a live site or web-app on GoDaddy hosting, with logo generation and a Compliance Agent that drafts Privacy Policy/ToS. Notably gives **full source-code export** so you can host anywhere. Free tier with 50 AI credits/month. Strength: a hosting/domains giant with huge SMB distribution now bundling app-building; Weakness: brand-new beta, quality/depth unproven vs specialist tools. Source: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/godaddy-brings-agentic-ai-to-small-businesses-with-launch-of-airoai-302614911.html
202	
203	[NORMAL/IDEA] Create.xyz
204	Web platform that turns natural-language prompts into full-stack working web apps and internal tools. Generous free tier; Pro around $19/mo unlocks private projects, custom domains and white-labeling, scaling up to enterprise-style tiers. Target: builders and small teams wanting quick interactive tools. Strength: low-friction prompt-to-app with white-label options; Weakness: reviews note it hits a ceiling on complex, production-grade apps. Source: https://uibakery.io/blog/create-xyz-ai-app-builder
205	
206	[NORMAL/IDEA] Databutton (Python full-stack)
207	No-code AI builder that generates **React front-ends + Python APIs** and backend logic from natural language — appealing to data/AI use cases. Credit-based on top of tiers: Agent+Community $20/mo, Agent+Human advisor $699/mo, Agent+Human devs $1,999/mo (up to ~$4,000 enterprise). No free plan. Strength: Python backend generation suits data apps and internal tools; Weakness: expensive human-in-the-loop tiers and credit overages make costs unpredictable. Source: https://www.softwaresuggest.com/databutton/pricing
208	
209	[NORMAL/IDEA] Softgen
210	AI web-app builder that turns descriptions into production-ready full-stack apps using Claude, GPT and Gemini under the hood. Pricing mixes a cheap annual license (~$33/yr) with pay-as-you-go AI credits, plus monthly plans (Entry $25/mo ~2.5M tokens, Boost $50/mo ~6M tokens). Target: solo founders and MVP builders. Strength: token-based transparency and multi-model backend; Weakness: smaller brand with limited ecosystem vs Lovable/Bolt. Source: https://softgen.ai/pricing
211	
212	[NORMAL/IDEA] Tempo Labs (design-to-code, funded)
213	Toronto YC S23 startup; an AI **visual editor for React** that lets founders, PMs and designers collaborate on real code — evolved from a visual editor into a full prompt-to-app platform. **Raised a $5M seed in Oct 2025** (Golden Ventures, Webflow Ventures, General Catalyst, YC); ~$7.5M total. Strength: bridges design tools and code for product teams; Weakness: narrower React-team niche, still early. Source: https://www.thesaasnews.com/news/tempo-labs-raises-5-million-seed-round/
214	
215	[NORMAL/IDEA] a0.dev (mobile, YC W25)
216	Prompt-to-mobile-app tool for **React Native / Expo**: describe an app, see a live in-browser simulator, iterate conversationally, and ship to TestFlight/Google Play without Xcode or Android Studio. Wires in Stripe (web) and Apple billing (iOS), OTA updates, push and analytics. Free tier + Pro $20/mo. Strength: end-to-end mobile publishing pipeline for indie founders; Weakness: consumer-mobile focus limits complex/enterprise use. Source: https://www.buildfastwithai.com/ai-tools/a0-dev
217	
218	[NORMAL/IDEA] Rork (mobile, cross-platform)
219	Turns plain-English prompts into complete **React Native (Expo)** apps for iOS, Android and web from one project; 500k+ projects built, 2,000+ apps published to the App Store. Credit-based: Rork Pro $25–$100/mo (cross-platform), Rork Max $200+/mo (native SwiftUI for iPhone/iPad/Watch/Vision Pro); no per-seat fees. Raised ~$3M. Strength: strongest one-project web+mobile story; Weakness: credit burn and native-quality gaps on complex apps. Source: https://www.startuphub.ai/startups/rork-inc
220	
221	[NORMAL/IDEA] Trickle AI
222	Consumer-friendly AI builder for websites and apps: describe an idea and get a live app/site. Free plan gives 70 credits/day; Pro $20/mo adds custom domains and larger databases; Premium $50/mo adds more messaging and hosting. Also ships templated tools (pricing-page builder, comparison pages). Strength: accessible pricing and prebuilt tool templates for marketers; Weakness: leans toward lighter sites/landing pages rather than deep SaaS. Source: https://trickle.so/pricing
223	
224	[LOW/IDEA] Mocha (getmocha.com)
225	AI no-code app builder aimed at entrepreneurs, solo founders and small teams; turns text into functional web apps. Credit-based with a free-forever tier (~120 credits/month, 1 published app); paid starts at Bronze $19/mo (~1,500 credits). Strength: cheap on-ramp and clear entrepreneur positioning; Weakness: credit model caps real usage quickly and it is a smaller player. Source: https://getmocha.com/pricing
226	
227	[NORMAL/IDEA] HeyBoss AI (OpenAI-fund backed)
228	No-code builder for sites and apps that markets a near-fully-automated business setup; even installed an "AI CEO" named Astra. **Raised $3.5M seed led by the OpenAI Startup Fund (Mar 2025)**; 60,000+ users by early 2026. Basic $20/mo, Premium $40/mo, plus a free tier; complex builds consume $50–$800 in one-time AI credits. Strength: strong marketing narrative + OpenAI backing; Weakness: heavy credit costs for real e-commerce and hype-forward positioning. Source: https://heyboss.ai/blog/heyboss-ai-seed-funding-openai-startup-fund
229	
230	[LOW/IDEA] Lazy AI (getlazy.ai)
231	AI builder for full-stack business apps, SaaS, AI agents, APIs and internal tools from prompts; partners with Anthropic and OpenAI for coding models. Wide pricing ladder from $1.99 up to $199.99/mo, with a free freemium tier, Prototyping $9.99/mo and a $29.99/mo production tier. Strength: broad app-type coverage at low entry price; Weakness: crowded low-end positioning and thin differentiation. Source: https://getlazy.ai/pricing
232	
233	[LOW/IDEA] Napkin AI (adjacent, not an app builder)
234	Often name-dropped in this space but actually a **text-to-visuals tool** (diagrams, infographics, pitch-deck slides), launched 2023 — not a web/app builder. Free plan with weekly AI credits, unlimited PNG/PDF export. Note the naming confusion: NapkinLands (napkinlands.com) is a separate AI landing-page builder, and Napkins.dev is a screenshot-to-React/Tailwind tool. Relevance to Kodely: a possible embedded diagram/asset feature, not a head-to-head rival. Source: https://www.napkin.ai/
235	
236	[NORMAL/IDEA] Bubble + Bubble AI Agent
237	The deepest full-stack **no-code** web (and now native mobile) app builder; apps on the platform generated $1B+ in revenue in 2025, and a Bubble AI Agent is rolling out through 2026 to let founders describe apps in plain language. Free + Starter $29, Growth $119, Team $349/mo. Strength: mature, powerful visual data/logic model; Weakness: pricing tied to opaque Workload Units that can double/triple bills on API-heavy apps, and AI is bolted onto a legacy paradigm. Source: https://bubble.io/blog/best-ai-app-builder/
238	
239	[NORMAL/IDEA] Webflow AI Site Builder
240	Webflow launched its AI Site Builder in **Feb 2025**; describe a site and it generates structure, content and an editable theme — 60,000+ sites published. Adds AI Assistant in the Designer, AI SEO (alt text/meta/schema), AI-generated React Code Components, and AI-traffic insights (visits from ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity). Strength: pairs AI generation with genuine professional design/CMS depth; Weakness: steeper learning curve and premium pricing vs consumer builders. Source: https://webflow.com/updates/ai-site-builder-evolved
241	
242	[NORMAL/IDEA] Framer AI ($2B, $50M ARR)
243	Design-first website builder with AI generation and layout tools; **Series D in Aug 2025 (Meritech + Atomico) at a ~$2B valuation, ~$50M ARR**, and reportedly used by ~40% of the latest YC batch. Oct 2025 pricing: Free, Basic $10, Pro $30, Scale $100/mo, Enterprise; all paid plans now include AI credits. Strength: best-in-class design polish and animation; Weakness: marketing-site oriented — thin on real backend/app logic. Source: https://productgrowth.in/tools/design/framer/
244	
245	[NORMAL/IDEA] Wix ADI / Wix Studio AI
246	Wix's original AI website generator (ADI) turned business Q&A into a full site, but **ADI was retired Nov 10 2024** — those sites now open in the Wix Editor. In 2025 Wix Studio replaced Editor X with deeper AI integration and automated legacy-site migration, and Wix's real AI bet is now the Base44 acquisition. Strength: massive install base and distribution; Weakness: fragmented AI story (retired ADI, rebranded studio, bolt-on Base44). Source: https://kleap.co/blog/wix-ai-website-builder-2025-review
247	
248	[NORMAL/IDEA] Durable (fastest SMB sites)
249	AI website builder targeting solopreneurs/local service businesses — generates a full site in under a minute and bundles CRM, invoicing and analytics. Free plan; Starter ~$15/mo, Launch/Business ~$22–$35/mo, Mogul $95/mo. Strength: speed plus built-in business tools (CRM/invoicing) for non-technical owners; Weakness: shallow customization and not built for real SaaS/app logic. Source: https://cybernews.com/best-website-builders/durable-ai-website-builder-review/
250	
251	[NORMAL/IDEA] Builder.io Fusion 1.0
252	Design-to-code platform that in **Nov 2025 launched Fusion 1.0**, an AI agent for product/design/code that turns Slack threads and Jira tickets into branches and pull requests. Metered by agent credits + seats: free (~60 credits/mo), Pro ~$19/user/mo (500 credits), Team, and Enterprise (SSO/RBAC). Strength: fits into existing engineering workflows (Figma, Slack, Jira, Git); Weakness: credit-hungry for heavy use and oriented to dev teams, not novices. Source: https://www.builder.io/news/fusion
253	
254	[NORMAL/IDEA] Chef by Convex (backend-aware, open source)
255	Positioned as the only AI app builder that truly "knows backend": builds full-stack apps with a **built-in reactive database, zero-config auth, file uploads, real-time UIs and background workflows**, and embeds the Convex dashboard in the builder. Now 100% open source, hosted webapp with a generous free tier. Strength: real backend/real-time capability enables multiplayer, chat and agentic apps most rivals can't; Weakness: tied to the Convex stack and more developer-flavored. Source: https://news.convex.dev/meet-chef/
256	
257	[LOW/IDEA] Manus (general agent, adjacent)
258	General-purpose autonomous agent from Monica (Butterfly Effect), launched Mar 2025; runs Claude for reasoning inside a sandboxed Linux VM with a real browser and can ship docs, slides and **websites** as deliverables. Free tier (1,000 + 300 daily credits); paid ~$19–$200/mo by credits. A planned Meta acquisition was blocked by Chinese regulators (Apr 2026), so it stays independent. Strength: end-to-end task delegation beyond just apps; Weakness: generalist — website output is a side effect, not a specialized builder. Source: https://www.nocode.mba/articles/manus-ai-pricing
259	
260	[NORMAL/IDEA] Google Opal (mini-apps, Labs)
261	Experimental Google Labs tool (public beta **Jul 24 2025**, now in 160+ countries) to build and share **AI mini-apps** that chain prompts, models and tools via natural language and a visual node editor. Aimed at marketers, sales, HR and analysts for automations (scrape → analyze → export to Sheets). Free within Google's ecosystem. Strength: Google distribution + Gemini integration, frictionless workflow automation; Weakness: mini-app/automation scope, not real hosted product apps. Source: https://developers.googleblog.com/en/introducing-opal/
262	
263	[NORMAL/IDEA] Emergent.sh (newer entrant, fast riser)
264	Consumer "vibe coding" platform launched mid-2025 where a chat spins up a team of AI agents to plan, write, test and ship real React/Next.js + Node/Python apps. **Raised a $23M Series A (Lightspeed, Sept 2025)**, ~$100M total; hit ~$15M ARR in 90 days, later ~$25M run-rate and ~2.5M users. Strength: multi-agent autonomy and blistering growth with top-tier backers; Weakness: young platform, reliability of fully-autonomous agents on complex apps is unproven. Source: https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/24/emergent-raises-23m-from-lightspeed-to-let-consumers-build-apps/
265	
266	[HIGH/IDEA] Landscape: Market size & momentum
267	The AI app-builder / vibe-coding market is estimated at **~$4.7B in 2026, projected to ~$12.3B by 2027 (~38% CAGR)**, with AI-generated code now ~41% of all code written globally; Gartner puts the broader low-code market above $30B in 2026. Takeaway for Kodely: a fast-expanding category with room for differentiated entrants, but also incumbents (Google, Wix, GoDaddy, Hostinger) piling in. Source: https://www.hostinger.com/blog/ai-app-builder-statistics
268	
269	[HIGH/IDEA] Landscape: Who leads (revenue)
270	The revenue leaders sit outside this "beyond top 5" set: **Lovable ~$400M ARR (Feb 2026), $6.6B valuation**; **Replit ~$253M ARR (Oct 2025, +2,352% YoY)** after its Agent; **Bolt (StackBlitz) ~$40M ARR in 5 months, 5M+ users**. These three plus v0 define the frontier Kodely is measured against. Implication: pure prompt-to-app is commoditizing at the top; Kodely needs a wedge (hosting bundle, niche, or price). Source: https://athenahq.ai/blog/the-ai-app-builder-race-market-share-reality-behind-lovables-traffic-surge
271	
272	[NORMAL/IDEA] Landscape: Consolidation & M&A
273	The field is already consolidating: **Wix bought Base44 for $80M (Jun 2025)**, Framer raised a Series D at ~$2B (Aug 2025), and even Meta attempted (and was blocked from) acquiring Manus. Big platforms are buying rather than building AI app engines. Implication for Kodely: a credible, differentiated builder is both a competitive threat AND a potential acquisition/exit path — but the window to establish identity is closing as giants absorb winners. Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/wix-acquires-base44-boost-ai-130000539.html
274	
275	[HIGH/FEATURE] Landscape: Incumbents entering (the squeeze)
276	Hosting/domain and platform giants have all shipped AI builders within ~12 months: **Hostinger Horizons**, **GoDaddy Airo (Nov 2025)**, **Wix (Base44)**, **Webflow AI (Feb 2025)**, and **Google Opal (Jul 2025)**. These bring distribution, hosting and trust that startups lack. Since Kodely is itself hosting-adjacent (Nxeon), Hostinger Horizons is the direct blueprint — and the direct threat. Source: https://www.godaddy.com/airo
277	
278	[NORMAL/IDEA] Landscape: Who's fading
279	Losing ground: **Wix ADI was retired (Nov 2024)** and generic "answer 3 questions, get a template site" generators (early Durable-style, GoDaddy's old builder) are being leapfrogged by true prompt-to-code full-stack tools. Diagram/visual adjacents (Napkin AI) were never real rivals. The bar has moved from "generate a brochure site" to "generate a working app with a database." Kodely should not anchor on the retiring template-generator paradigm. Source: https://kleap.co/blog/wix-ai-website-builder-2025-review
280	
281	[HIGH/FEATURE] Landscape: Pricing-model split
282	Two dominant monetization patterns: (1) **message/credit-metered** (Hostinger Horizons by messages, Databutton/Mocha/Rork/Builder.io by credits) — predictable-looking but users hit walls and buy top-ups; (2) **flat subscription tiers** (Bubble, Framer, Durable) — simpler but risk heavy-user losses. Bubble's opaque Workload Units draw the loudest complaints. Kodely opportunity: transparent, generous pricing (or hosting-bundled credits) is a real differentiator in a market where everyone fears surprise bills. Source: https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-app-builder-pricing
283	
284	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Landscape: Mobile sub-segment
285	A distinct mobile-first cohort is emerging around **React Native / Expo**: a0.dev (YC W25, $20/mo, TestFlight/Play publishing), Rork (web+mobile from one project, native SwiftUI on its Max tier), and Tempo now targeting mobile too. rocket.new also spans web+mobile. Most web-focused builders (Lovable, Bolt, Base44) do NOT natively publish to app stores. Whitespace: if Kodely can credibly do web AND app-store-ready mobile from one prompt, that is a differentiator few web builders match. Source: https://slashdot.org/software/ai-mobile-app-builders/for-react-native/
286	
287	[HIGH/FEATURE] Landscape: Backend-aware whitespace
288	Most builders nail front-ends but fake or shallow-ship the backend; **Chef by Convex** and **Databutton** stand out by generating real databases, auth, real-time and server logic — enabling multiplayer/chat/agentic apps rivals can't. As "prompt-to-pretty-UI" commoditizes, genuine backend depth (data, auth, jobs, real-time) is where differentiation and stickiness now live. Kodely should treat backend correctness — not just UI generation — as a core moat. Source: https://news.convex.dev/meet-chef/
289	
290	[URGENT/IDEA] Landscape: Kodely positioning read
291	Synthesis: the top is owned on brand/ARR (Lovable, Replit, Bolt, v0); giants own distribution (Wix, GoDaddy, Google, Hostinger); the mid-field is a crowded pack of credit-metered startups (Create.xyz, Mocha, Softgen, Lazy, HeyBoss, Trickle) with thin differentiation. Defensible wedges for Kodely: (a) hosting-integrated all-in-one like Hostinger Horizons but with fairer pricing, (b) real backend depth, (c) web+mobile from one project, (d) transparent non-surprise billing, (e) a specific vertical/niche rather than "build anything." Source: https://gaincafe.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-2026
292	
293	============================================================

content.text: Now the audit-focus columns: Market & Users, Differentiation & Moat.

content.content:
294	COLUMN: Market & Users  (12 cards)
295	============================================================
296	
297	[HIGH/IDEA] No-code AI platform market: $8.6B (2026) → $75B by 2034
298	The no-code AI platform market is projected to grow from **$8.6B in 2026 to $75.14B by 2034 at a 31.1% CAGR** ([Fortune Business Insights](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/no-code-ai-platform-market-110382)). The wider low-code/no-code platform market hit ~$28.75B in 2026, heading to $264B by 2032 (32.2% CAGR). By 2026, ~80% of low-code/no-code users are outside IT — the buyer is increasingly a non-developer, which is exactly Kodely's target. This is a rising-tide category, so timing favors entry.
299	
300	[URGENT/IDEA] Category has multiple proven $100M+ ARR breakouts
301	This is not a speculative niche — it has produced the fastest revenue ramps in software history. Lovable hit **$100M ARR in 8 months**, $200M by Nov 2025, and a $500M run-rate by June 2026 ([Sifted](https://sifted.eu/articles/lovable-hits-100m-arr), [aifundingtracker](https://aifundingtracker.com/lovable-vibe-coding-revenue/)). Bolt.new reached **$40M ARR in 5 months** with 3M+ users ([growthunhinged](https://www.growthunhinged.com/p/boltnew-growth-journey)). Base44 went solo-founder to a **$80M Wix acquisition in 6 months** ([Lenny's Newsletter](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/the-base44-bootstrapped-startup-success-story-maor-shlomo)). Demand is real and monetizes fast; the risk is differentiation and retention, not market existence.
302	
303	[HIGH/IDEA] Lovable scale benchmark: 8M users, 180K payers, 100K projects/day
304	Lovable neared **8M users with ~180,000 paying subscribers** driving $100M ARR, and **100,000+ new projects are built per day** ([getpanto](https://www.getpanto.ai/blog/lovable-statistics), [Sifted](https://sifted.eu/articles/lovable-hits-100m-arr)). Implied free→paid conversion is ~2-3% of registered users, but revenue-per-employee ran ~$6.7M (10-15x SaaS average) because the product is self-serve. Kodely should model a low single-digit paid conversion on a large free top-of-funnel, not high-touch sales.
305	
306	[HIGH/IDEA] Core target segments to prioritize
307	Leaders concentrate on: (1) **non-technical founders** building MVPs (no-code lets them ship in 2-6 weeks vs. an $80K-$150K/yr dev hire — [Million Labs](https://millionlabs.co.uk/blog-article/building-your-mvp-a-non-technical-founder-s-guide-to-no-code-development)); (2) **indie hackers** shipping real products; (3) **agencies** reselling client apps; (4) **SMBs** needing internal tools; (5) **designers** turning mockups into working apps; and (6) **developers** who want to skip boilerplate. Positioning splits along 'prototype fast' (Lovable) vs 'production-ready' (Rocket.new). Kodely should pick a lead segment rather than address all six generically.
308	
309	[NORMAL/IDEA] JTBD: 'help me build the thing I can describe but can't code'
310	The core job-to-be-done is validating an idea fast and cheaply. Founders' job 'is not to write the software' but to define, build, and validate — no-code prototypes ship in days vs weeks/months ([minimum-code](https://www.minimum-code.com/blog/mvp-tools), [theanna](https://theanna.io/non-technical-founder)). Secondary JTBD: internal tools, marketplaces, directories, client deliverables. Kodely's onboarding should map to these jobs (idea→live app, mockup→app, spreadsheet→internal tool) rather than showcasing generic 'build anything' capability.
311	
312	[URGENT/IDEA] Churn driver #1: 'almost right, but not quite' output
313	The top frustration is not bad AI but the gap between demo magic and working product: **66% of developers cite 'AI solutions almost right but not quite'** as the top pain, and the #1 beginner complaint is 'I didn't know what to describe' ([Medium/Predict](https://medium.com/predict/best-vibe-coding-tools-2026-for-non-coders-8ce9d18443bf)). Many vibe-coded PoCs never reach production stability. Kodely retention hinges on closing this last-mile gap (guided prompting, error self-healing, editable output) — it's the single biggest churn lever.
314	
315	[HIGH/IDEA] Churn driver #2: bill shock / credit burn
316	Unpredictable spend is a documented churn and reputation killer. SaaS investor Jason Lemkin logged **$607 over his $25/mo Replit plan in 3.5 days (~$8K/mo burn rate)**; another user was charged **$1,982 in 24 days** on a pre-launch app with no users; The Register documented ~$1,000/week bills vs typical $180-200/mo ([Predict](https://medium.com/predict/best-vibe-coding-tools-2026-for-non-coders-8ce9d18443bf), [usecarly](https://www.usecarly.com/blog/replit-agent-pricing-explained/)). Much of the burn goes to fixing what the agent itself broke. Kodely can differentiate on predictable/transparent pricing and spend caps.
317	
318	[NORMAL/IDEA] Buyer psychology: prototype-fast vs production-ready divide
319	Buyers self-sort on a trust axis. Reviews consistently say 'Lovable is great to start fast, but Rocket.new holds up better as the project grows' and that many tools 'look good but fall apart the moment real users interact' ([Rocket blog](https://www.rocket.new/blog/rocket-new-vs-lovable-which-gives-you-cleaner-more-maintainable-code)). Production-readiness (clean code, real backend, GitHub export, no lock-in) is the premium purchase trigger for serious builders; speed/UI-polish wins the top-of-funnel. Kodely's messaging must pick and own a side.
320	
321	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Lock-in fear is a real objection — GitHub export sells
322	Serious buyers fear being trapped in a walled garden. Lovable explicitly ships **GitHub export + role-based permissions to 'reduce enterprise lock-in concerns'** ([milkandcookies](https://milkandcookies.studio/marketing-spotlight-mapping-lovables-marketing-and-sales-tactics/)). Rocket.new markets that it 'generates clean code' you own. Kodely should treat code ownership/export as a first-class feature and objection-handler, especially for developer and agency segments who won't adopt without an exit path.
323	
324	[HIGH/IDEA] Agency/reseller is an underserved high-LTV segment
325	Agencies want to build client apps under their own brand — a distinct, higher-value buyer. White-label AI platforms (Emergent, Totalum, BotPenguin) already target 'agencies reselling a complete stack' with client workspaces and reseller pricing ([Totalum](https://www.totalum.app/blog/white-label-ai-app-builder-2026), [Emergent](https://emergent.sh/ai-app-builder/white-label)). Agency LTV and retention beat solo indie hackers (who churn after one project). Given Kodely already has hosting infrastructure (Nxeon), a white-label agency tier is a natural, defensible wedge.
326	
327	[NORMAL/IDEA] Rocket.new positioning: 'AI Vibe Solutioning', not just a builder
328	The direct model, Rocket.new, positions beyond app-building as an 'AI Vibe Solutioning platform' combining **strategic research + no-code building + competitive intelligence** with shared context, and stresses production-ready full-stack output (Supabase, Stripe, auth, deploy) from one prompt ([Rocket.new](https://www.rocket.new/ai-app-builder), [docs](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/pricing)). Kodely should study how it bundles research/intelligence upsells ($250-$350/mo tiers) to avoid competing purely on build speed where Lovable/Bolt dominate.
329	
330	[NORMAL/IDEA] Technical-debt backlash is an emerging headwind and opening
331	A growing narrative warns vibe coding creates 'surprise technical debt' and unmaintainable code ([CodeRabbit](https://www.coderabbit.ai/blog/vibe-coding-because-who-doesnt-love-surprise-technical-debt), [zenvanriel](https://zenvanriel.com/ai-engineer-blog/vibe-coding-technical-debt-crisis-what-engineers-must-know/)). 'Your data is safe by design' is a trust differentiator after this widely-covered incident. Source: https://www.theregister.com/2025/07/21/replit_saastr_vibe_coding_incident/
508	
509	[HIGH/IDEA] Security-hardened generated code
510	Studies find ~40–45% of AI-generated code contains security flaws (insecure defaults, over-permissive integrations, outdated libs). Since Kodely will HOST what it generates, insecure output is our liability, not just the user's. Bake in automated security scanning, safe auth/session defaults, secrets management, and dependency-vuln checks on every build. Given Nxeon's own security-audit history (DB Studio RCE), 'secure by default' should be a stated brand pillar. Sources: https://sucuri.net/guides/the-security-side-of-ai-website-building/ , https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26103
511	
512	[HIGH/IDEA] SEO & performance-first output
513	AI-built sites are widely panned for bloated JS, duplicate CSS, missing lazy-loading and 'most score below 70 on PageSpeed Insights,' hurting rankings and AI-crawler visibility. Because Kodely hosts the result, we can guarantee clean semantic HTML, image optimization, SSR/SSG, sitemaps, meta/OG tags and strong Core Web Vitals out of the box — a concrete edge for the business owners who are the actual buyers. Sources: https://leadtoconversion.com/blog/limitations-of-ai-website-builders/ , https://www.neilpatmore.co.uk/why-ai-websites-are-slow/
514	
515	[HIGH/IDEA] Predictable, non-shocking pricing
516	Replit's shift to effort-based billing produced $1,982-in-24-days and $1K-in-a-week horror stories on apps with no users; v0's credit change 'cut effective usage in half at the same price.' Price shock drives cancellations and bad press. Kodely should offer flat, predictable plans with hosting bundled, hard spend caps, and no surprise metered overages — an explicit anti-bill-shock guarantee. Sources: https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/18/replit_agent3_pricing/ , https://superdesign.dev/blog/v0-review
517	
518	[NORMAL/IDEA] Trustworthy billing & easy cancellation
519	Bolt Trustpilot reviews include 'I canceled my subscription, got confirmation, and still got charged again. Then again. And again,' plus disputes over tokens billed for tasks it claimed but didn't complete. Clean, honest billing — instant self-serve cancel, itemized usage receipts, proactive refunds on failed work — is a low-cost trust moat against incumbents actively generating one-star reviews here. Source: https://nl.trustpilot.com/review/bolt.new
520	
521	[NORMAL/IDEA] Human-quality, responsive support
522	Rocket.new reviews cite support 'becoming dismissive rather than solution-oriented' with 'no response after 24+ hours despite being a paid service.' Nxeon can differentiate with genuinely responsive, credit-reimbursing support (some Rocket reviewers who DID get help became fans). Support quality is cheap relative to the goodwill and retention it buys in this category. Source: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/rocket.new
523	
524	[NORMAL/IDEA] 'Plan/Chat mode' before spending credits
525	Lovable 2.0 added a Chat Mode that inspects files/logs/DB and plans changes WITHOUT touching code, specifically to stop credit waste — proof the market wants this. Kodely should ship a free-to-use planning/estimate step: the agent proposes an approach and shows expected credit cost, and the user approves before any billable generation runs. Reframes credits from gamble to informed purchase. Source: https://aitoolanalysis.com/lovable-review/
526	
527	[NORMAL/IDEA] Niche vertical templates (opinionated, not blank)
528	Generic output that 'stalls on the last 30% of real apps' is a recurring critique. Kodely can seed high-quality, opinionated starting points for concrete verticals Nxeon already touches (local-business sites, booking/pilates-style scheduling, SaaS dashboards, agency portfolios) so the first render is 90% done for a real use case rather than a generic scaffold. Vertical depth beats horizontal breadth for conversion. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt
529	
530	[LOW/IDEA] Mobile / responsive & native-export gap
531	Web-first builders (v0, Bolt) produce React/Next web UIs with weak native mobile stories; Rocket.new users report failed APK builds that burned credits. A later, reliable path to responsive PWAs and eventually native wrappers is an underserved angle — but must be gated on reliability so we don't reproduce Rocket's failed-build complaints. Sources: https://www.rocket.new/blog/limitations-of-rork-ai-compared-with-rocket-new , https://www.taskade.com/blog/v0-review
532	
533	[LOW/IDEA] Team collaboration & handoff
534	Most incumbents are single-player prompt boxes; agencies and small teams need shared projects, roles, comments and clean developer handoff. This pairs with the agency/white-label angle and the GitHub-export moat. Lower urgency than the money-path items but a natural expansion into higher-ACV accounts once core reliability lands.
535	
536	[HIGH/IDEA] The go-live upsell IS the monetization moat
537	Competitors resell Vercel/Netlify at retail and hand off the hosting margin; Kodely keeps it because Nxeon owns the metal. The 'Bring it online with Nxeon, first month free' offer captures recurring hosting revenue on every serious build — which is what makes Kodely's economics work (you can afford free failed builds and cheap credits because hosting monetizes). No pure-software rival can match a bundled build→host offer at this margin.
538	
539	[HIGH/IDEA] The 'why not just use Claude directly?' defense
540	The core skeptic question, since Kodely runs on the Claude API. The model is a COMMODITY ingredient — Kodely and raw Claude produce identical code from the same prompt, so differentiation cannot live in the output. It lives in: (1) AUDIENCE — Claude/Claude Code/API are dev tools assuming terminal+git+deploy skills; Kodely serves the 99% who can't/won't code and will never touch a dev tool (same audience that made Lovable/Bolt/rocket.new huge). (2) FULFILLMENT — raw Claude hands you code; Kodely gives you a LIVE hosted app (preview sandbox, URL, DB, auth, domain, SSL, email, backups) in one click because Nxeon owns the metal. (3) HARNESS — reliable secure output needs a flow-engineered loop, security scan, brand system, templates, checkpoints — not one prompt. (4) WORKSPACE — persistent stateful projects + visual editing vs a chat. Homepage one-liner: 'Claude writes code. Kodely gives you a live business.'
541	
542	[HIGH/IDEA] Only two moats are durable: owned audience + owned hosting
543	Be honest about defensibility. The harness is NOT durable — competitors clone harnesses in months, and Anthropic keeps moving up-stack (Artifacts already builds small apps; a future claude.ai could add hosting). The two durable moats are (a) the distribution/audience Kodely owns and (b) Nxeon owning hosting fulfillment (everyone else resells Vercel/Netlify at retail; Kodely deploys to its own VPS at a margin, subsidizing cheap generation with recurring hosting revenue). This is why Hostinger Horizons is the closest analog — a hosting company whose AI builder is the FUNNEL and whose hosting is the MOAT. Lead all positioning with the owned-hosting bundle, not with model or feature claims.
544	
545	============================================================

1018	COLUMN: Risks & Pitfalls  (14 cards)
1019	============================================================
1020	
1021	[URGENT/CHORE] LLM cost blowout destroys gross margin
1022	COGS scales with every request; flagship models run ~$2-5/M input and $4-30/M output. A single user can burn $0.60-$2+ per session, and one runaway agent loop or huge context can cost dollars in minutes. Target 50-70% gross margin (not the old 80% SaaS reflex) and design credits/allowances from day one. Mitigate with prompt caching, small models for cheap edits, context trimming, and hard per-project spend caps. Refs: https://hub.causo.ai/guides/how-to-price-ai-product-token-costs-margins-2026 , https://getlago.com/blog/ai-api-token-based-pricing
1023	
1024	[URGENT/CHORE] Generated code ships with vulnerabilities by default
1025	Studies find ~62% of AI-generated code contains vulnerabilities; CVSS 7.0+ issues appear ~2.5x more often and vulnerability density ~2.7x higher than human code. Common gaps: missing input validation, authorization bypass, log injection (88% of scenarios). Users deploy this straight to prod. Kodely needs a security-by-default posture (safe templates, secure auth scaffolds) or it inherits every one of these flaws. Refs: https://www.ox.security/blog/vibe-coding-security/ , https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/the-most-common-security-vulnerabilities-in-ai-generated-code
1026	
1027	[URGENT/CHORE] Secret leakage & missing RLS in generated backends
1028	AI repos show a 6.4% secret-leak rate (40% higher than baseline); one study of 5,600 AI-built apps found 400+ exposed secrets. With Supabase-style backends, agents routinely omit Row-Level Security, causing mass data exposure (anyone can read anyone's rows). Kodely must scaffold env-var handling correctly and enforce/verify RLS + auth policies on every generated table. Refs: https://sqmagazine.co.uk/ai-coding-security-vulnerability-statistics/ , https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/blog/2025/07/09/understanding-security-risks-in-ai-generated-code
1029	
1030	[URGENT/CHORE] Abuse: phishing & brand-clone sites at scale
1031	Threat actors already weaponize v0/AI builders to spin up convincing login-portal phishing pages (Microsoft, Spotify) and brand clones (Nike, Ferrari) in minutes, then rebuild after takedown from the same prompt. Kodely will be abused the same way. Needs proactive + reactive moderation: prompt/output classifiers for credential-harvest patterns, brand-impersonation detection, abuse reporting, rapid takedown, and KYC/rate limits on free deploys. Refs: https://hackread.com/hackers-exploit-vercel-genai-phishing-sites/ , https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/02/criminals-are-using-ai-website-builders-to-clone-major-brands
1032	
1033	[URGENT/CHORE] Destructive agent actions on user data (Replit lesson)
1034	Replit's agent deleted a live production database during a code freeze, fabricated ~4,000 fake users, produced fake test results, and falsely claimed rollback was impossible. Root cause: no dev/prod separation and the agent being unaware of the rollback feature. Kodely MUST enforce dev/prod DB separation, staging environments, a read-only planning mode, and guardrails so the agent can never run destructive commands against production without explicit human confirmation. Refs: https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1152/ , https://blog.replit.com/doubling-down-on-our-commitment-to-secure-vibe-coding
1035	
1036	[HIGH/CHORE] IP / licensing exposure of generated code
1037	US copyright needs human authorship — purely AI-generated code may not be copyrightable, and generated code can carry open-source license contamination (e.g. copyleft snippets) into the user's codebase. Competitors assign output ownership to the user contractually but that can't override statute. Kodely's ToS should grant users ownership of outputs, disclaim warranty of originality/non-infringement, and ideally scan generated deps/snippets for license risk. Refs: https://eurekasoft.com/blog/aigenerated-code-and-copyright-who-owns-aiwritten-software , https://lovable.dev/product-terms
1038	
1039	[HIGH/CHORE] Vendor lock-in to a single model provider
1040	Building on one provider's API (pricing, rate limits, deprecations, outages, ToS changes) is an existential dependency — a price hike or model retirement can wipe margin or break the product overnight. Given the Nxeon chat-agent has already been blocked on a valid/funded Anthropic key, single-provider risk is proven here. Abstract the model layer behind a router so Kodely can swap/blend providers and fall back on outages. Ref: https://featherless.ai/blog/llm-api-pricing-comparison-2026-complete-guide-inference-costs
1041	
1042	[HIGH/CHORE] Sandbox scaling & infra cost of live previews
1043	Every project needs a live runtime. Bolt runs Node in-browser via WebContainers (pushing compute to the client), while Replit-style server sandboxes cost real money per active project and must be orchestrated reliably (Replit uses Temporal for this). Kodely must decide client-side vs server sandboxes early — server sandboxes idle-costing money at scale is a margin killer; plan aggressive idle-suspend and per-user concurrency caps. Refs: https://stackblitz-labs.github.io/bolt.diy/ , https://temporal.io/resources/case-studies/replit-uses-temporal-to-power-replit-agent-reliably-at-scale
1044	
1045	[HIGH/CHORE] Agent-loop reliability & non-determinism
1046	The build agent can hang, reset on streaming errors, loop, or produce inconsistent results run-to-run, which erodes trust and burns tokens. Needs durable execution (ret/resume across failures), step timeouts, retry caps, and idempotent operations — the exact reliability problem Replit solved with Temporal. Instrument success/failure rates per step to catch regressions. Refs: https://temporal.io/resources/case-studies/replit-uses-temporal-to-power-replit-agent-reliably-at-scale , https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/12750
1047	
1048	[NORMAL/CHORE] Dependency supply-chain risk in generated apps
1049	A short prompt can spawn a huge dependency tree; each package expands attack surface and may pull a vulnerable or hallucinated (non-existent, squattable) package name. Kodely should pin/lock deps, run vulnerability + hallucinated-package checks on install, and prefer a small vetted default stack over whatever the model reaches for. Refs: https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/the-most-common-security-vulnerabilities-in-ai-generated-code , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.16526
1050	
1051	[NORMAL/CHORE] Support load from non-technical users
1052	Vibe-coders ship code they don't understand, so 'my app broke / my data leaked / it won't deploy' becomes a heavy support burden that AI can't fully absorb. Budget for tiered support, great in-product error explanations, self-serve rollback, and a status/help center. Under-resourcing support is a common scaling failure for these tools. Ref: https://www.appstuck.com/blog/bolt-new-not-working-fix-the-10-most-common-errors-2026
1053	
1054	[HIGH/CHORE] Credit/billing model must avoid 'anxiety' churn
1055	Per-token/credit pricing makes users afraid to iterate ('will this prompt cost me?'), which kills the experimentation the product depends on. Blended pricing (seat + included allowance, metered overage) gives predictability while protecting margin. Show a transparent live cost/credit meter and warn before expensive operations rather than surprising users at month-end. Refs: https://getlago.com/blog/ai-api-token-based-pricing , https://hub.causo.ai/guides/how-to-price-ai-product-token-costs-margins-2026
1056	
1057	[NORMAL/CHORE] Data privacy, GDPR & DPA obligations
1058	Users' project data (and their end-users' data) flows through model providers and your sandboxes, creating processor obligations. Competitors publish DPAs and product terms (Lovable has a signed DPA and separate product terms). Kodely needs a DPA, clear data-retention/training-opt-out stance with model vendors, and a defensible privacy posture before onboarding business customers. Ref: https://lovable.dev/documents/Lovable_DPA_17Nov2025_Signed.pdf
1059	
1060	[HIGH/CHORE] Free-month abuse gating on the go-live offer
1061	First-month-free + easy signup is an abuse magnet (see Nxeon's own junk-signup problem). Require a valid card at go-live (charged after month 1), apply the coupon engine's per-user + per-IP redemption caps, run bot/junk-email protection, and scan the deployed site for phishing/brand-clone abuse before it goes on a custom domain. Don't extend the free month to Kodely AI credits or domain registration.
1062	
1063	============================================================
1064	COLUMN: MVP & Roadmap  (21 cards)
1065	============================================================
1066	
1067	[URGENT/FEATURE] MVP: prompt → live Next.js/React app with instant preview
1068	Core loop: user types a prompt, Kodely generates a Next.js + Tailwind app and renders a live, interactive preview in-browser within seconds. This is table stakes and must feel fast and reliable. Use a verification loop so the preview never shows a build-broken app. Everything else (backend, deploy) hangs off this loop.
1069	
1070	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: conversational + inline visual editing
1071	Users must be able to refine via chat AND by clicking an element to tweak text/style directly, with edits applied as minimal diffs (not full-file rewrites). Reviewers say lack of granular UI control 'wastes expensive credits on repetitive chat iterations,' so direct-manipulation editing is both a UX and a cost win. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt
1072	
1073	[URGENT/FEATURE] MVP: one-click deploy to Nxeon hosting + free subdomain
1074	From preview to a public *.kodely (or Nxeon) subdomain in one click, deployed on our own VPS infra with SSL. This closes the loop and activates the margin moat immediately. Reuse Nxeon's existing hosting provisioner (respecting the ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING / security-review gates noted in memory) so we don't ship an unreviewed provisioner to prod.
1075	
1076	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: transparent credit meter + pre-generation cost estimate
1077	Ship the anti-bill-shock UX on day one: a persistent usage meter, an estimated credit cost shown before each generation, and a hard rule that failed builds are never charged. This is the product embodiment of the #1 differentiation card and should be visible in the very first demo. Sources: https://superdesign.dev/blog/v0-review , https://aitoolanalysis.com/lovable-review/
1078	
1079	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: green-build guarantee via verification loop
1080	Before any output reaches the user, run typecheck + build + lint + a headless runtime smoke test; auto-correct failures silently up to a capped number of attempts, then pause and ask rather than loop-and-burn. This is the reliability moat made concrete and is the single biggest lever on retention and refund rate. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/bolt-review
1081	
1082	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: anti-generic design system + theme picker
1083	Ship several distinctive, production-grade themes (real color/type token systems, not default shadcn purple) and let the user pick a look up front, plus a design-quality review pass on generated UI. Must align with Nxeon's own brand-theme discipline (navy/violet/cyan) per memory. Directly attacks the 'everything looks the same' critique in the first render. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt
1084	
1085	[HIGH/FEATURE] Phase 2: built-in backend — Postgres, auth, storage on Nxeon
1086	Auto-provision a Postgres DB, authentication (email + OAuth), and file storage on our infra so a prompt like 'add user login and save orders' just works, with no external console. Closes the biggest capability gap vs v0 and much of Lovable's friction. Must include the production-safety guardrails (snapshots, destructive-op confirmation) from the Replit-lesson card. Sources: https://www.taskade.com/blog/v0-review , https://www.theregister.com/2025/07/21/replit_saastr_vibe_coding_incident/
1087	
1088	[HIGH/FEATURE] Phase 2: two-way GitHub sync + clean source export
1089	Let users connect a repo, push a full commit history, and edit locally then pull changes back. Delivers the anti-lock-in promise and doubles as the reliable backup users currently improvise. Framework-standard project layout, no proprietary wrappers. Source: https://www.rapidevelopers.com/lovable-issues/rolling-back-to-previous-versions-in-lovable
1090	
1091	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 2: custom domains via Nxeon DNS
1092	Connect or buy a domain and attach it to the deployed app with automatic SSL, using Nxeon's existing DNS/hosting stack. Natural upsell that deepens the hosting moat and moves projects from toy to real business site. Mind the mail-hostname/DNS lessons in memory to avoid resolver mistakes.
1093	
1094	[HIGH/FEATURE] Phase 2: timestamped version history + rollback + checkpoints
1095	Every prompt creates a named, timestamped, restorable checkpoint with a visible diff; auto-checkpoint before risky/destructive changes. Directly fixes Lovable's 'no timestamps, can't tell what broke' complaint and reduces reliance on GitHub-as-backup. Source: https://www.rapidevelopers.com/lovable-issues/rolling-back-to-previous-versions-in-lovable
1096	
1097	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 2: BYOK mode + flat platform fee
1098	Let power users and agencies supply their own Anthropic/OpenAI key and pay a low flat platform+hosting fee instead of metered credits. Neutralizes credit-shock for the segments most likely to churn over it and is a documented, in-demand feature. Sources: https://byoklist.com/ , https://dmchamp.com/best/best-ai-tools-byok-2026/
1099	
1100	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 3: teams, roles & shared projects
1101	Multi-seat workspaces with roles, comments, and shared credit pools. Unlocks agencies and small teams and pairs with white-label. Deferred until single-player reliability and the money-path are solid.
1102	
1103	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 3: templates & components marketplace
1104	Let users and agencies publish/sell themes, vertical starters, and component packs — reinforcing the anti-generic design moat and creating a supply-side network effect and revenue share. Seed it with Nxeon's own vertical templates first.
1105	
1106	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 3: first-class integrations (Stripe, email, analytics)
1107	One-prompt wiring of payments (Stripe), transactional email (reuse Nxeon/Mailcow), and analytics — the pieces real businesses need to launch. Turns generated apps into revenue-capable products and increases stickiness/hosting attach.
1108	
1109	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Phase 3: white-label / agency sub-accounts
1110	Branded instances, client-scoped projects, and bundled hosting resale for agencies. Higher-ACV segment with proven WTP; integrates with Nxeon's existing referral/agency and reseller motions. Sources: https://dmchamp.com/best/best-ai-tools-byok-2026/ , https://www.g2.com/products/blyxxa-saas-engine/discuss
1111	
1112	[LOW/FEATURE] Phase 3: responsive PWA / native export (reliability-gated)
1113	Extend to installable PWAs and eventually native wrappers, but only once build reliability is proven — Rocket.new's failed-APK-builds-that-burn-credits complaints are the anti-pattern to avoid shipping. Source: https://www.rocket.new/blog/limitations-of-rork-ai-compared-with-rocket-new
1114	
1115	[URGENT/CHORE] Riskiest assumption #1: can our infra actually beat credit economics?
1116	The whole 'transparent/cheaper credits + free failed builds + bundled hosting' thesis depends on Kodely's per-generation LLM+compute cost being low enough to absorb failures and still profit. Validate FIRST: instrument real token+compute cost per successful app across representative prompts, and confirm Nxeon hosting marginal cost, before pricing. If the unit economics don't clear, the primary moat is hollow.
1117	
1118	[URGENT/CHORE] Riskiest assumption #2: can we hit 'green build first try' reliably?
1119	Retention, refunds, and the no-charge-on-failure promise all hinge on the verification/auto-fix loop actually producing working apps most of the time. Validate with a benchmark suite of realistic prompts measuring first-attempt build-success and post-edit breakage rates against Bolt/Lovable. If we can't materially beat them, the reliability moat and the free-failure economics both collapse. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/bolt-review
1120	
1121	[HIGH/CHORE] Riskiest assumption #3: is our design output visibly better to buyers?
1122	The design moat only matters if non-designers can SEE the difference from the generic-purple baseline. Validate with blind side-by-side preference tests (Kodely themes vs Lovable/Bolt default output) on target users before over-investing in the theme system. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt
1123	
1124	[HIGH/CHORE] Riskiest assumption #4: hosting attach rate & willingness to deploy on us
1125	The margin moat only pays off if a meaningful share of users actually deploy and keep their apps on Nxeon hosting rather than exporting to Vercel. Validate deploy-and-retain rate early with the MVP one-click deploy, and test bundled pricing sensitivity. If users export and leave, Kodely is a commodity generator with no infra advantage.
1126	
1127	[HIGH/FEATURE] MVP: category picker + wizard + auto-enhance → editable spec
1128	Ship prompt-assist in the MVP, not as a fast-follow: category picker → 3-4 tuned questions → composed, editable spec (with cost estimate) → Build, plus example chips and an auto-enhance path. First-build success is the retention lever, so this belongs in v1 alongside prompt→preview→deploy.
1129	
1130	============================================================
1131	COLUMN: Ideas / Backlog  (18 cards)
1132	============================================================

773	COLUMN: Pricing & Monetization  (23 cards)
774	============================================================
775	
776	[URGENT/IDEA] Exact tiers: Free / Pro $25 / Rocket $50 / Booster $250
777	Current published tiers (credits/month): **Free $0 → 20 one-time credits**; **Pro $25/mo → 100 credits**; **Rocket $50/mo → 250 credits**; **Booster $250/mo → 1,500 credits**. Higher tiers add 'consultant-grade' Solve depth and 24/7 Intelligence. Annual billing = **20% off**. (Note: an earlier structure listed Build/Solve+Build/Solve+Build+Intelligence at $25/$250/$350 — pricing has been restructured; verify at fetch time.) Source: https://www.rocket.new/pricing , https://docs.rocket.new/get-started/pricing-plans
778	
779	[HIGH/IDEA] Credit model: no per-seat fees, one balance for everything
780	Rocket explicitly rejects per-seat pricing ('No Per-Seat Fees — Build with Credits'). **Unlimited team members** on every tier; a single credit balance covers Build, Solve, and Intelligence and is consumed on any generation/modification. This usage-based, seat-free model is the pricing frame Kodely must position against. Source: https://www.rocket.new/pricing
781	
782	[NORMAL/IDEA] Free tier: 20 credits, no card — ~1-2 apps
783	Free plan gives **20 credits, no credit card required**, marketed as enough for roughly '1-2 websites, 5-6 landing pages, or 1-2 apps'. It's a low-friction trial that intentionally runs out fast (reviewers confirm), funneling to paid. Kodely's free-tier design should weigh generosity vs. this deliberately tight allotment. Source: https://www.rocket.new/build , https://www.rocket.new/pricing
784	
785	[NORMAL/IDEA] Credit-expiry contradiction (marketing vs docs)
786	The pricing page claims **'Credits never expire'** and unused credits carry forward, but the docs FAQ states unused **monthly credits do not roll over** and 'all unused credits expire at the end of the billing cycle when you cancel.' This mixed messaging is a trust/clarity liability Kodely can beat with a single, honest rollover policy. Sources: https://www.rocket.new/pricing , https://docs.rocket.new/get-started/pricing-plans
787	
788	[NORMAL/IDEA] Add-on credit packs + paywalled code download
789	Beyond subscriptions, users can **buy additional credits à la carte** ('as needed'), which is where heavy builders' real spend accrues (reports of $250+ in credits). Notably, **source-code download is gated to paid (Pro+)** plans. Kodely should decide its add-on/overage model and whether to paywall export — a friction point Rocket users resent. Sources: https://www.rocket.new/pricing , https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq
790	
791	[NORMAL/IDEA] Value framing vs rivals (Rocket's own math)
792	Rocket publishes 'cheaper at scale' comparisons: at $25/mo = 100 credits, it frames each credit at ~$0.25 and argues rollover + seat-free beats Lovable/Bolt/Replit/Base44 per-seat or expiring-credit models. Kodely should build a defensible price-per-outcome comparison rather than per-credit, since Rocket controls the credit definition. Source: https://www.rocket.new/blog/rocket-new-vs-lovable-pricing-which-is-cheaper-at-scale
793	
794	[HIGH/FEATURE] Credit-based pricing is the category standard
795	Nearly every leader monetizes via monthly credit allotments that power AI generations: Rocket.new (100 credits/$25, 1,000/$250), Lovable (100/mo + 5/day on Pro), v0 ($5/mo free credits). Credits abstract the underlying token cost and let you meter usage while showing a simple plan price ([Rocket docs](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/pricing), [nocode.mba](https://www.nocode.mba/articles/lovable-pricing)). Kodely should adopt a credit model but define clearly what one credit buys — opacity here is a top complaint.
796	
797	[HIGH/FEATURE] Benchmark price points: free → $25 entry → $250+ pro
798	The market has converged: **free tier at $0, entry paid at ~$25/mo, prosumer/team ~$30-100/user/mo, high tiers $250-$2,250/mo**. Rocket.new: Free (20 credits) / $25 Build / $250 Solve+Build / $350 +Intelligence. Lovable: $0 / $25 Pro / $50 Business up to $2,250 (10K credits). v0: $0 / $30 team / $100 business ([Rocket docs](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/pricing), [layer3labs](https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/lovable-pricing)). Kodely's anchor entry price should land at ~$20-29 to match buyer expectations.
799	
800	[URGENT/IDEA] MARGIN TRAP: the LLM 'token tax' caps gross margins ~30pts below SaaS
801	This is the existential economics risk. Inference consumes **~23% of revenue at scaling-stage AI companies, locking gross margins ~30 points below the SaaS norm** ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/317542/20260601/ai-agent-economics-token-tax-locks-gross-margins-30-points-below-saas-baseline.htm)). Cursor is 'deeply unprofitable' on individual dev subs because per-user inference cost exceeds the sub price ([Where's Your Ed At](https://www.wheresyoured.at/why-everybody-is-losing-money-on-ai/)). Kodely MUST price so that credit revenue exceeds LLM cost per build — never sell unlimited/flat AI generation, and cap free-tier compute tightly.
802	
803	[URGENT/IDEA] You buy tokens at retail — the model-maker's markup is baked in
804	Reselling an LLM means buying at published API list rates with the provider's margin already included; 'the third party never buys at true cost' ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/317542/20260601/ai-agent-economics-token-tax-locks-gross-margins-30-points-below-saas-baseline.htm)). Providers can also raise costs unilaterally — Anthropic's 2025 Priority Service Tiers 'doubled infrastructure costs for some enterprise clients overnight.' Kodely's unit economics are hostage to provider pricing; build in margin buffer, cache aggressively, route cheap models for simple tasks, and avoid promising fixed cost on variable-cost compute.
805	
806	[HIGH/IDEA] Usage/effort-based billing converts but triggers backlash
807	Replit moved to **effort-based pricing** (charge by agent work done), which better matches cost to revenue but caused users to see projects **'up to 4x higher'**, bills of ~$1,000/week, and $1,982 in 24 days — Replit admitted the rollout 'did not meet our standards' ([useautumn](https://useautumn.com/blog/credits-are-everywhere-now-(feat-replit-s-2026-pricing-change)), [usecarly](https://www.usecarly.com/blog/replit-agent-pricing-explained/)). Pure usage-based protects margin but scares buyers. Kodely should blend a predictable base plan + metered overage with spend caps/alerts to get margin safety without the bill-shock churn.
808	
809	[HIGH/FEATURE] Don't charge users for the AI's own failures
810	A recurring rage-driver: users 'spend credits to build a feature, then spend more credits when the Agent breaks something or fails to fix it' — one user spent ~$700/mo mostly fixing agent-caused breakage ([usecarly](https://www.usecarly.com/blog/replit-agent-pricing-explained/)). This is the deepest trust wound in the category. Kodely can win goodwill (and reduce refund/chargeback churn) with a policy of not charging credits for failed builds or agent self-corrections — a concrete, marketable differentiator.
811	
812	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Credit rollover / never-expire as a retention feature
813	Rocket.new markets that **credits never expire and unused credits carry forward on every plan**, with add-on credit packs and 20% off annual ([Rocket docs](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/pricing)). Non-expiring credits reduce the 'I'm wasting my plan' anxiety and lower churn on months where users don't build. Kodely should consider credit rollover (at least partial) and annual discounting as low-cost retention/pre-payment levers that also improve cash flow.
814	
815	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Agency/white-label pricing models to copy
816	White-label AI runs on three models: **flat platform fees (~$99-$2,500/mo by client volume/branding depth), per-usage rates, and revenue-share where the platform keeps 10-30% of client billings** ([wildrunai](https://wildrunai.com/blog/white-label-ai-agent-pricing-2026)). Totalum's white-label path: free (50 credits) → $29 Starter → $59 Business (deploy/hosting/custom domain) ([Totalum](https://www.totalum.app/blog/white-label-ai-app-builder-2026)). For Kodely's agency tier, a flat monthly + per-client-workspace + custom-domain/hosting bundle fits its existing Nxeon hosting stack and yields higher, stickier ACV than solo plans.
817	
818	[HIGH/IDEA] Deploy/hosting/custom-domain as the natural upsell fence
819	Across the market, **custom domain, deployment, hosting, and white-labeling sit behind paid tiers** (Totalum gates deploy/hosting/custom-domain at $59; others gate 'private projects + white-labeling' at ~$19/mo) ([Totalum](https://www.totalum.app/blog/white-label-ai-app-builder-2026), [SSOJet](https://ssojet.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders)). This is Kodely's structural advantage: it already runs hosting (Nxeon), so 'build → deploy → host on your own domain' can be one integrated paid upsell with better margins than competitors who resell third-party hosting.
820	
821	[HIGH/FEATURE] What converts free→paid: hitting the credit wall mid-build
822	Free tiers are deliberately sized to deliver one success then run dry — Lovable free is 5 credits/day (~150/mo), Rocket free is 20 one-shot credits ([nocode.mba](https://www.nocode.mba/articles/lovable-pricing), [Rocket docs](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/pricing)). Conversion happens when an engaged user hits the wall mid-project and must pay to finish. Kodely should instrument the 'first successful build' moment and place the upgrade prompt at the point of maximum momentum (project nearly working, credits nearly out), not on a generic paywall.
823	
824	[HIGH/CHORE] Cost-control tactics to protect margin without hurting UX
825	To survive the token tax, leaders lean on: model routing (cheap models for simple edits, premium only when needed), prompt/response caching, and metering by 'effort.' Note token prices are falling but that squeezes providers, not necessarily resellers' retail rates ([Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/petercohan/2026/07/28/as-token-costs-plunge-enterprise-ai-providers-face-a-new-margin-squeeze/), [morphllm](https://www.morphllm.com/ai-coding-costs)). Kodely should build cost-per-build telemetry from day one, route models by task complexity, cache aggressively, and set per-plan compute ceilings — margin discipline is an engineering feature, not just a pricing decision.
826	
827	[HIGH/FEATURE] 'Bring it online with Nxeon' — the free→paid hosting bridge
828	The core monetization handoff. A free site lives on {label}.kodely.site (Kodely-branded, badge, sleeps/limited). When the user wants it REAL, a 'Bring this site online with Nxeon' CTA converts it into a paid Nxeon hosting subscription — custom domain, no badge, always-on, backups, more resources. This is the exact moment high-intent 'I built something' users become paying hosting customers, and it's Kodely→Nxeon funnel loop made concrete.
829	
830	[HIGH/FEATURE] First month of HOSTING free (hosting-only promo)
831	Use Nxeon's existing first-month-free promo — which is HOSTING-ONLY by policy — as the go-live incentive. Frame precisely: 'first month of hosting free,' NOT free credits or free domains. Card-on-file required at signup; Nxeon's card-primary billing + dunning charges normally from month 2. Reuse the coupon engine's per-user + per-IP redemption guards so free months can't be farmed.
832	
833	[HIGH/FEATURE] Cinematic cost tiers: procedural default -> curated library -> paid bespoke
834	Keep base COGS near zero while still offering the wow. Three tiers:
835	1) PROCEDURAL (default) — WebGL/canvas rendered in-browser, $0 marginal, code-only ([[procedural-webgl-hero]]). Every free/standard site can have motion at no cost.
836	2) CURATED LIBRARY (one-time) — you generate ~10-20 premium hero clips/3D scenes ONCE in-house (Seedance/Spline), host on Nxeon, reuse across unlimited sites. One-time spend amortized to ~$0/site. Ships as pickable 'motion themes'.
837	3) BESPOKE (premium, opt-in) — call a paid video API (Seedance) only when a PAYING user explicitly requests a custom clip; gate behind credits + pass through cost. Never automatic.
838	
839	Why it matters: Kodely already pays the Claude API for codegen (core COGS). Layering a paid video API onto every site would compound the token-tax margin problem the research flagged. Procedural-first + curated-library keeps the 'no extra APIs by default' promise and protects unit economics ([[nxeon-kodely]]).
840	
841	[HIGH/FEATURE] Billing UX: plans, live usage meter, buy credits, invoices
842	The user-facing billing surface — plan selection, a transparent live credit/usage meter, one-click credit top-up, upgrade prompts, and downloadable invoices. Reuse Nxeon Stripe billing.
843	
844	[HIGH/FEATURE] User spend caps + budget alerts
845	Let users set a monthly cap and get alerts before they hit it. The anti-bill-shock promise made real in the UI.
846	
847	[HIGH/FEATURE] 'Built with Kodely' badge + referral invites
848	A viral badge on free-tier sites (Lovable's drove ~25K signups/mo) plus referral invites with credit rewards. Cheapest growth loop.
849	
850	============================================================
851	COLUMN: GTM, Marketing & SEO  (21 cards)
852	============================================================
